title: Contractual Hiring and Compensation Knowledge Check — Building the Project Team: Contractual Hiring and Compensation
display_label: Contractual Hiring and Compensation Knowledge Check — Building the Project Team: Contractual Hiring and Compensation
content:
Contractual Hiring and Compensation Knowledge Check

From the ORA eTraining module "Building the Project Team: Contractual Hiring and Compensation" (lesson 14 of 15).
incorrect
Knowledge check: A faculty principal investigator earns $115,000 on a 9.5-month academic contract and has three active awards with a combined $40,000 available for salary support. What is the maximum amount the PI can earn in summer salary?
  - $40,000  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - $30,245  [incorrect]
  - $29,900  [incorrect]
  - $23,958  [incorrect]
  Note on "$40,000": Even if the total salary budgeted across a faculty member's sponsored awards exceeds the allowable summer limit, the faculty member may not earn more than 26.3% of their 9.5-month contract salary during the summer period.
  Note on "$30,245": Great job!
  Note on "$29,900": Remember that the maximum amount a 9.5-month faculty member can earn across all summer funding is 26.3% of their 9.5-month contract salary.
  Note on "$23,958": Remember that the maximum amount a 9.5-month faculty member can earn across all summer funding is 26.3% of their 9.5-month contract salary.
Knowledge check: Which Banner pool level is used for employing contractual staff?
  - 02  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - 04  [incorrect]
  - 09  [incorrect]
  - 11  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  If correct: Great job!
  If incorrect: Try again.
  Note on "02": Great job!
  Note on "04": This is the Travel Banner pool
  Note on "09": This is the Supplies Banner pool
  Note on "11": This is the Equipment Banner pool
Knowledge check: Employees can begin working on a grant as soon as the notice of award is at Morgan and the budget is setup in Banner.
  - True  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - False  [incorrect]
  If correct: Great job!
  If incorrect: Please remember that employees may not begin work until their contract is signed and fully authorized by Morgan's HR Office.
Knowledge check: What system should be utilized to submit a grant-funded employment contract for a new employee?
  - DocuSign (PF-10)  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - EPAF  [incorrect]
  - Canvas  [incorrect]
  - ARGOS  [incorrect]
  Note on "DocuSign (PF-10)": Remember: PF-10s should only be used for existing contract revisions.
  Note on "EPAF": Great job!
  Note on "Canvas": Try again.
  Note on "ARGOS": Try again.
Knowledge check: An admin tries to submit an EPAF contract but realizes they do not have access to the EPAF system. What should they do?
  - Hold the contract  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - Submit a PF-10 instead  [incorrect]
  - Request EPAF access through Workflow  [incorrect]
  - Email ORA Budget Officers  [incorrect]
  If correct: Great job
  Note on "Hold the contract": We want our employees to start as soon as possible so they can contribute meaningfully to our sponsored awards. Please reach out to hris@morgan.edu if you have concerns regarding EPAF access.
  Note on "Submit a PF-10 instead": Contracts should be entered with plenty of lead time for approval processing. EPAF access requests are fast moving so please request access prior to submitting a PF-10 instead.
  Note on "Request EPAF access through Workflow": Great job!
  Note on "Email ORA Budget Officers": ORA Budget Officers are here to help, but they cannot provide this access. You should instead speak with your School's Budget Officer for access assistance.
Knowledge check: Which of the following is required before entering an EPAF contract?
  - detail code  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - effort reporting account  [incorrect]
  - contractual PIN  [incorrect]
  - ORA Budget Officer approval  [incorrect]
  If correct: Great job!
  If incorrect: Try again.
Knowledge check: When can multiple employees share the same contractual PIN?
  - Always  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - Never  [incorrect]
  - Same Project & Same Position Title  [incorrect]
  - Same Supervisor  [incorrect]
  If correct: Great job!
  If incorrect: Try again.
Knowledge check: What is the maximum work limit for student employees during the academic year?
  - 10 hours/week  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - 20 hours/week  [incorrect]
  - 35 hours/week  [incorrect]
  - 40 hours/week  [incorrect]
  If correct: Great job!
  If incorrect: Try again.
Knowledge check: A PI earns $89,000 per year on a 9.5-month faculty academic contract. If the summer period includes 53 working days, what would the PI's hourly rate be for summer contracts?
  - $55.20  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - $62.15  [incorrect]
  - $55.21  [incorrect]
  - 42.78  [incorrect]
  Note on "$55.20": Great job!
  Note on "$62.15": Try again.
  Note on "$55.21": You need to round hourly rates down instead of up. It is better to have a dollar or two left over in a budget than to overspend it.
  Note on "42.78": Remember this employee is not paid over 12 months (2080 hours per year for full time).
Knowledge check: A student is receiving federal stipend support. Can they also be hired to work on the grant?
  - Yes  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - No  [incorrect]
  - Only with PI approval  [incorrect]
  - Only part-time  [incorrect]
  If correct: Great job!
  If incorrect: Try again.
Knowledge check: A PI has $10,000 budgeted in direct costs for salary and fringe on summer contracts. What is the salary portion?
  - $10,000  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - $9,100  [incorrect]
  - $9,174  [incorrect]
  - $7,042  [incorrect]
  If correct: Great job! $10,000 / 1.09 = $9174.31
  If incorrect: Try again.
Knowledge check: Which department processes fully approved Special Compensation requests?
  - Office of Research Administration  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - Payroll  [incorrect]
  - Accounts Payable  [incorrect]
  - Human Resources  [incorrect]
  Note on "Office of Research Administration": ORA is a part of the Special Compensation approval process. They do not authorize the completed document for payment.
  Note on "Payroll": Great job!
  Note on "Accounts Payable": Accounts Payable is not involved in the Special Compensation process.
  Note on "Human Resources": HR is not involved in the Special Compensation process.
